source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, first two middle paragraphs: induction on the nilpotence exponent, then the largest x-nilpotent submodule and the x-injective quotient. The uniform exponent and homogeneity are the explicit graded finite-generation argument in the returned eight-step proof.

proof.text: For every finite graded module $V$ under consideration, choose finite generators and replace them by all their homogeneous components $v_j\in V_{a_j}$. Their $S$-span contains the original generators, so still equals $V$. Choose degree-one algebra generators $z_1,\ldots,z_t$ using [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Projecting a generating expression to degree $n$ shows that $V_n$ is spanned by the monomials $z_1^{e_1}\cdots z_t^{e_t}v_j$ with $\sum e_i=n-a_j$. There are finitely many such tuples, also when $t=0$; hence every $V_n$ is finite-dimensional.

source.place: Tag 00K0, lemma-graded-module-fg, homogeneous-generator monomial argument preceding 00K1.

proof.text: Prove the first assertion by induction on $r\ge1$, simultaneously for all finite graded $L$ with $x^rL=0$. The case $r=1$ is the hypothesis. For $r>1$ put $A=xL$ and $B=L/xL$. Images under multiplication by $x$ of finite generators generate $A$, and images of generators of $L$ generate $B$. If $l=\sum l_n$, then the degree-$n$ component of $xl$ is $xl_{n-1}$ (zero for $n=0$). Thus $A$ is graded with $A_n=xL_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$ and $A_0=0$. Give $B$ the grading $B_n=\operatorname{im}(L_n\to B)$: every element is a sum of such images; if a sum of homogeneous representatives lies in $A$, each component lies in $A$, proving directness. Scalar multiplication respects these degrees. We have $x^{r-1}A=0$ and $xB=0$.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, first middle paragraph: explicit choice of the smaller-exponent modules.

proof.text: For each $n$, the maps induced by inclusion and quotient give $0\to A_n\to L_n\to B_n\to0$: the last map is onto by the definition of $B_n$, and its kernel is $L_n\cap A=A_n$. Step 1 makes these spaces finite-dimensional. A basis of $A_n$ together with arbitrary lifts of a basis of $B_n$ is a basis of $L_n$: projecting proves independence of the lifted vectors modulo $A_n$, and subtracting their linear combination leaves an element of $A_n$. By the induction hypothesis applied to $A$ with exponent $r-1$ and the original hypothesis applied to $B$, choose eventual polynomials $P_A,P_B$ and thresholds $d_A,d_B$. Therefore $P_L=P_A+P_B$ works for $n\ge\max(d_A,d_B)$. This completes the induction, including zero modules.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, nilpotent induction and degreewise additive relation.

proof.text: Now let $M$ be any finite graded module and put $T=\{m:\exists r\ge1,\ x^rm=0\}$. It contains zero. If $x^am=0$ and $x^bn=0$, then $x^{\max(a,b)}(m+n)=0$, and for $s\in S$, commutativity gives $x^a(sm)=s(x^am)=0$; additive inverses are treated the same way. Thus $T$ is an $S$-submodule. If $m=\sum m_n\in T$ with $x^rm=0$, its summands $x^rm_n$ have distinct degrees $n+r$, so directness implies $x^rm_n=0$ for every $n$. Consequently $T=\bigoplus_n(T\cap M_n)$ is graded.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, second middle paragraph: construction and homogeneity of the largest nilpotent submodule.

proof.text: Since $S$ is Noetherian and $M$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] applied to the submodule $T\subseteq M$ proves that $T$ is a finite $S$-module. These are exactly the ring and module hypotheses of the cited statement.

source.place: Tag 00IK, lemma-Noetherian-basic, second assertion, used to justify the largest nilpotent submodule in 00K1.

proof.text: Choose generators $t_1,\ldots,t_h$ of $T$. For each $j$ choose $r_j\ge1$ with $x^{r_j}t_j=0$, and set $r=\max(\{1\}\cup\{r_j:1\le j\le h\})$. Then $x^rt_j=0$ for every generator, hence $x^rT=0$ by $S$-linearity. The already proved nilpotent assertion applies to the finite graded module $T$ and gives $P_T$ and $d_T$. If $T=0$ the empty generating list permits $r=1$ and $P_T=0$.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, largest nilpotent submodule: uniform exponent made explicit using finite generators.

proof.text: Images of finite generators of $M$ generate $N=M/T$. Put $N_n=\operatorname{im}(M_n\to N)$. The sum of these subspaces is all of $N$; if $\sum m_n\in T$, step 4 gives $m_n\in T$ for each $n$, proving that the sum is direct. For $s\in S_i$ and $m\in M_j$, $s\overline m=\overline{sm}\in N_{i+j}$, so this is the asserted quotient grading. Finally, if $x\overline m=0$, then $xm\in T$; some $a\ge1$ satisfies $x^a(xm)=0$. Thus $x^{a+1}m=0$, so $m\in T$ and $\overline m=0$. Multiplication by $x$ on $N$ is injective. For $x=0$ this says $T=M$ and $N=0$, as required.

source.place: Tag 00K1, proposition-graded-hilbert-polynomial, second middle paragraph: quotient by the largest nilpotent submodule has injective x-action.

title: Nilpotent devissage and bounded homogeneous power torsion
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $S=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S_n$ be a standard graded $k$-algebra [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra] which is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and fix $x\in S_1$. A nonnegatively graded $S$-module $L=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}L_n$ means a direct sum of $k$-subspaces with $S_iL_j\subseteq L_{i+j}$; finite means finitely generated as an $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Assume that for every such finite $L$ satisfying $xL=0$ there are $P_L\in\mathbf Q[X]$ and $d_L\in\mathbf N$ with $\dim_kL_n=P_L(n)$ for all $n\ge d_L$. Then the same conclusion holds for every finite nonnegatively graded $L$ satisfying $x^rL=0$ for some integer $r\ge1$. Moreover, for every finite nonnegatively graded $S$-module $M$, the subset $T=\{m\in M:\exists r\ge1,\ x^rm=0\}$ is a finite graded $S$-submodule, with grading $T_n=T\cap M_n$, and there is a single integer $r\ge1$ such that $x^rT=0$. There are $P_T\in\mathbf Q[X]$ and $d_T\in\mathbf N$ with $\dim_kT_n=P_T(n)$ for all $n\ge d_T$. The quotient $N=M/T$, graded by $N_n=\operatorname{im}(M_n\to M/T)$, is finite and multiplication by $x$ on $N$ is injective. Zero modules and the zero polynomial are allowed.
